onboarding.consentIntro: Please review how we handle your health information.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.body: Health Journal gives health information and organizes your records. It is not a doctor, pharmacist or emergency service.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.body: Your data is private to your account, encrypted in transit and at rest, and stored by Supabase in Frankfurt, Germany. You can export or delete it at any time.

health_data_processing.title: Storing your health information
health_data_processing.body: We store the health records, documents and medications you add so the app can track them over time.

ai_processing.title: AI reading and explanations
ai_processing.body: Lets the app send your documents and relevant records to a secure AI model to read reports and answer your questions. Your data is not used to train AI models. Without it, you can still enter results yourself.

scan.title: Scan a report
scan.subtitle: Take a photo of a lab report or upload a PDF. You'll check everything before it's saved.
scan.limits: JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF · up to 20 MB and 20 pages
scan.readingHint: This usually takes under a minute. You can leave this screen; the report will wait for you in Records.
scan.savedOther: Your document is saved. Reviewing prescriptions and doctor reports comes in a later update.
scan.duplicate: You've already uploaded this exact file.
scan.enterManuallyHint: Type values from a paper report. No AI is used.
scan.uploadError: The upload didn't complete. Check your connection and try again.

invalid.type: This file type isn't supported. Use a JPEG, PNG, WebP image or a PDF.
invalid.size: This file is larger than 20 MB.

start.consent_required: AI reading isn't allowed for your account. Allow it above, or enter results manually.
start.quota_exceeded: You've reached this month's limit of 30 scanned documents. You can still enter results manually.
start.ai_not_configured: Report reading isn't set up yet. Your file is saved; try again later or enter results manually.
start.error: We couldn't start reading this report. Your file is saved; try again.

failure.ai_unavailable: The reading service is unavailable right now. Your file is saved; try again.
failure.timeout: Reading is taking longer than expected. Check Records in a few minutes.
failure.ai_refused: This document couldn't be read automatically. Enter the results manually.
failure.document_too_long: This document is too long to read in one go. Try uploading fewer pages.
failure.invalid_ai_output: The reading result was incomplete. Try again.
failure.save_failed: We read the report but couldn't save the draft. Try again.
failure.file_missing: The uploaded file couldn't be found. Upload it again.
failure.too_many_pages: This PDF has more than 20 pages. Upload only the pages with results.
failure.unreadable: We couldn't read this document. Try a clearer, well-lit photo.
failure.ai_busy: The reading service is busy. Try again in a minute.
failure.ai_not_configured: Report reading isn't set up yet. Try again later.
failure.ai_rejected_file: This file couldn't be processed. Try a different photo or PDF.
failure.image_too_large: This photo is too large to read. Try a photo with a lower resolution, or a PDF.

review.title: Check your results
review.subtitle: Results that were read clearly are listed at the bottom. Only the ones below need your check.
review.duplicate: A confirmed report from the same date has almost identical results. If this is the same report, discard this copy.
review.dateFallback: Only a report date was found, so it is used as the collection date. I've checked this date.
review.dateUncertain: The day and month order on this report may be ambiguous. I've checked this date.
review.unitNotComparable: This unit can't be converted to {{unit}}, so this result won't be compared with your other results for this test.
review.unmatchedHint: Not in the app's list. It will still be tracked by its printed name and unit. Pick the test if you know it; the app will remember it next time.
review.checkedAgainstDoc: I've checked the highlighted fields against the document

problems.name: Every result needs a test name.
problems.unchecked: Check the highlighted fields and tick the box under each one.

review.saveError: Saving didn't work. Nothing was changed; try again.
review.discardConfirm: Discard this report? Its draft results won't be saved.
review.notFound: This report isn't available for review.
review.aiMatchUnit: Looks like {{test}}, but the unit doesn't fit that test. Pick the test if you're sure.

report.sourceNote: Values come from your confirmed report. Status labels compare each value with the range printed by the lab; they are not a diagnosis.
report.notComparable: Not compared: the unit or date can't be matched with your other results.
report.byNameOnly: Compared by printed name and unit only: this test isn't in the app's list yet.
report.unrecognized: Not in the app's list yet. Future results with the same name and unit will be compared with this one.
report.removeConfirm: Remove this result from your record? The original is kept in the change history.
report.correctionNote: The original value is kept in the change history. All comparisons will use the corrected value.

liver.borderline: Borderline elevation ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). On its own this doesn't establish liver injury; worth discussing with your doctor at your next visit.
liver.mild: Mild elevation ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). Discuss with your doctor, who may suggest repeating the test.
liver.moderate: Moderate elevation ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). Contact your doctor soon to review this result.
liver.severe: Marked elevation ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). Contact your doctor promptly today.
liver.massive: Very high result. Seek medical care today.

history.notFound: No results found for this test.
history.noNumeric: This test has no numeric results to chart.
history.notCompared: Not included (different unit that can't be converted)
history.changesNote: Shown for context. A change around the same time doesn't mean it caused a change in your results.

chart.summary: Chart of {{count}} results from {{first}} to {{last}}. Latest: {{value}}.
chart.bandNote: Shaded band: the normal range printed on your latest report. Tap a point for details; tap again to open its report.

compare.title: Compare reports
compare.subtitle: Two report dates side by side. Changes are calculated by the app, not by AI.
compare.needTwo: Confirm at least two lab reports to compare them.

insights.title: Insights
insights.subtitle: What stands out in your confirmed results, with the values and dates behind each point.
insights.empty: Nothing stands out in your confirmed results right now.
insights.disclaimer: Insights are calculated by the app from your confirmed results and published guidelines. They are health information, not a diagnosis. Dismissing an insight never changes your results.

level.urgent: Urgent medical attention may be needed

critical_value.title: {{test}} needs prompt medical attention
critical_value.body: Your {{test}} of {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} is beyond a limit that laboratories treat as critical.
critical_value.action: Contact your doctor today. If you feel unwell, call {{emergency}} or go to the nearest emergency department.

outside_range_high.title: {{test}} is above the lab's range
outside_range_high.body: {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} (lab range {{range}}). A single result outside the range is common and is not a diagnosis on its own.
outside_range_high.action: Mention it at your next doctor visit.

outside_range_low.title: {{test}} is below the lab's range
outside_range_low.body: {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} (lab range {{range}}). A single result outside the range is common and is not a diagnosis on its own.
outside_range_low.action: Mention it at your next doctor visit.

ldl_severe_190.title: LDL cholesterol is 190 mg/dL or higher
ldl_severe_190.body: Your LDL of {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} is in the range that cholesterol guidelines treat as severely high.

hba1c_diabetes_range.title: HbA1c is in the diabetes range
hba1c_diabetes_range.body: {{value}}{{unit}} on {{date}} is 6.5% or higher, the range used to diagnose diabetes. One result is not a diagnosis: guidelines require a confirming test.

hba1c_prediabetes_range.title: HbA1c is in the prediabetes range
hba1c_prediabetes_range.body: {{value}}{{unit}} on {{date}} is between 5.7% and 6.4%, the range guidelines call prediabetes.
hba1c_prediabetes_range.action: Worth discussing at your next doctor visit.

egfr_category.title: Kidney filtration (eGFR) is in category {{category}}
egfr_category.body: {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}}. Category {{category}} means kidney filtration is lower than normal.
egfr_category.action: Discuss it with your doctor, who may repeat the test.

trend_improving.title: {{test}} has improved
trend_improving.body: From {{previousValue}} on {{previousDate}} to {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} ({{percent}}). The change is larger than normal day-to-day variation.

trend_worsening.title: {{test}} has moved further from the lab's range
trend_worsening.body: From {{previousValue}} on {{previousDate}} to {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} ({{percent}}). The change is larger than normal day-to-day variation.
trend_worsening.action: Worth discussing at your next doctor visit.

rules.screen_lung: Lung screening: ask if it's right for you

intervals.months3: guidelines suggest about every 3 months while treatment is changing or above goal

vitals.title: Readings
vitals.subtitle: What you measure at home: blood pressure, blood sugar, weight, heart rate, oxygen and temperature.
vitals.notePlaceholder: e.g. after a walk, felt dizzy

invalid.blood_pressure: Enter both numbers; the top number must be higher than the bottom one.
invalid.heart_rate: Enter a heart rate between 20 and 250.
invalid.oxygen: Enter an oxygen level between 50 and 100%.

vitals.oneReading: One reading doesn't diagnose anything. Doctors look at averages over several days.
vitals.childNote: The blood pressure categories here are for adults. Children's ranges depend on age and height; ask their doctor.
vitals.addHeight: Add height in the profile to see BMI.

band.blood_pressure: Shaded: normal and elevated range for the top number (90–129).
band.glucose: Shaded: usual target before meals for people with diabetes.
band.heart_rate: Shaded: normal resting range for adults (60–100).

empty.blood_pressure: No blood pressure readings yet. Measuring at the same time each morning gives the most useful average.
empty.weight: No weight entries yet. Once a week is enough.
empty.heart_rate: No heart rate readings yet. Measure at rest, at the same time of day.

meaning.bp_normal: This reading is in the normal range for adults.
meaning.bp_elevated: Slightly above normal. Healthy habits help keep it from rising; mention it at your next check-up if your average stays here.
meaning.bp_stage1: In the range doctors call stage 1 high blood pressure. Don't judge by one reading: if your average stays here, discuss it with your doctor.
meaning.bp_stage2: In the range doctors call stage 2 high blood pressure. If your average stays here, contact your doctor soon.
meaning.bp_severe: Very high. Wait 5 minutes and measure again. If it's still this high, contact your doctor right away. If you also have chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness or weakness, vision changes or trouble speaking, call emergency services now.
meaning.bp_low: Lower than usual. If you feel dizzy, faint or unwell, contact your doctor.
meaning.glucose_very_low: Very low blood sugar. Treat it now as your care team taught you, for example 15 g of fast-acting sugar (like half a cup of juice), then check again in 15 minutes. If you feel confused, can't eat or drink, or don't improve, get emergency help.
meaning.glucose_low: Low blood sugar. Have some fast-acting sugar and check again in 15 minutes. If this happens often, tell your doctor.
meaning.glucose_very_high: Very high. Contact your doctor today. If you're vomiting, very thirsty, drowsy or confused, get urgent care.
meaning.glucose_in_target: Within the usual target for people with diabetes at this time of day.
meaning.glucose_above_target: Above the usual target for this time. If many readings are like this, discuss it with your doctor.
meaning.glucose_fasting_raised: A fasting level of 100–125 mg/dL can be a sign of prediabetes. One home reading doesn't diagnose it; ask your doctor about a lab test.
meaning.glucose_fasting_high: A fasting level of 126 mg/dL or more is in the diabetes range. One home reading doesn't diagnose it; contact your doctor for a lab test.
meaning.glucose_high_random: 200 mg/dL or more at any time is high. Contact your doctor, especially if you're very thirsty or passing urine often.
meaning.bmi_under: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the underweight range.
meaning.bmi_healthy: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the healthy range.
meaning.bmi_over: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the overweight range. BMI doesn't account for muscle; your doctor can tell you what it means for you.
meaning.bmi_obesity: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the obesity range. BMI doesn't account for muscle; your doctor can tell you what it means for you.
meaning.hr_normal: A normal resting heart rate for adults.
meaning.hr_low: Below 60 at rest. This can be normal for fit people or with some medicines. If you feel dizzy, faint or short of breath, contact your doctor.
meaning.hr_high: Above 100 at rest. Rest for a few minutes and measure again. If it stays high or you feel chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath, contact your doctor; with chest pain or fainting, call emergency services.
meaning.spo2_normal: In the usual range. If your doctor gave you a different target, follow theirs.
meaning.spo2_borderline: 93–94% is a little lower than usual. Warm your hands, sit still and measure again. If it stays here or you feel unwell, contact your doctor. If your doctor gave you a different target, follow theirs.
meaning.spo2_low: 92% or lower: contact your doctor today. Measure again with warm hands first. Readings can be less accurate on darker skin, cold fingers or with nail polish. If your doctor gave you a different target (e.g. for COPD), follow theirs.
meaning.temp_fever: 38°C (100.4°F) or above is a fever. Rest and drink fluids. Contact your doctor if it lasts more than 3 days, or if you feel very unwell.
meaning.temp_very_high: 40°C (104°F) or above is a high fever. Contact your doctor today. Get urgent help if there's confusion, a stiff neck, a rash that doesn't fade under a glass, or trouble breathing.
meaning.temp_fever_baby: A baby under 3 months with 38°C (100.4°F) or above needs urgent medical advice now. For older babies, contact their doctor.
meaning.temp_low: Below 35°C (95°F) can be dangerous (hypothermia). Measure again; if it's still this low, get urgent medical help, especially for older people and babies.
meaning.spo2_very_low: 88% or lower: get immediate medical attention, especially if you're short of breath, confused, or your lips look bluish.

vitals.restingHint: Measure after sitting quietly for 5 minutes.

photo.button: Read from a photo of your device
photo.hint: Blood pressure monitor, glucose meter, oximeter, thermometer or scale. The photo isn't saved.
photo.check: Check these numbers match your device's screen, then save.
photo.checkLow: Some digits were hard to read. Please check every number carefully before saving.

errors.not_a_device: That doesn't look like a health device's screen. Try a closer photo of the display.
errors.unreadable: The numbers couldn't be read clearly. Try again with less glare, closer to the screen.
errors.several_devices: More than one screen is visible. Take a photo of just one device.

checkin.title: How are you today?
checkin.redFlag: Chest pain or shortness of breath can be serious. If it's severe, sudden, or comes with sweating, nausea or pain spreading to the arm or jaw, call emergency services now.

family.title: Family
family.subtitle: Keep records for people you care for. Each person's records stay separate.
family.settingsHint: Add a parent or family member and switch between them
family.removeWarning: This permanently deletes all of {{name}}'s records, documents, medicines and reminders. It cannot be undone.
family.removeError: Couldn't remove this person. Please try again.
family.name: Name
family.consentNote: Only add someone whose health information you're allowed to manage, for example with their agreement or as their carer.
family.limit: You can keep records for up to 10 people.
family.privacyNote: Family members' records are private to your account, like your own. Reminders for them say "someone you care for", never their name or medicine.

summary.title: Visit summary
summary.subtitle: One page to show your doctor: medicines, readings, results and your questions.
summary.shareNote: Sharing sends this summary to the app you choose (e.g. WhatsApp). Only share it with people you trust.
summary.outOfRange: Latest lab results outside the lab's range
summary.questionsPlaceholder: Write what you'd like to ask…
summary.footer: Prepared by the person with Health Journal from their own records and home readings. Not a medical document.

install.title: Add Health Journal to your Home Screen
install.whyIos: On iPhone, medicine reminders only work when the app is on your Home Screen. It takes 10 seconds.
install.why: Open it in one tap, like any app, and get reminders reliably.
install.ios1: In Safari, tap the Share button
install.ios3: Open Health Journal from your Home Screen and turn on reminders

visits.deleteConfirm: Delete this visit and its reminders?

voice.title: Say it
voice.examples: For example: "My blood pressure is 130 over 85", "I took my metformin", "Fasting sugar 110", "I started walking every day", "I have a headache".
voice.confirm: Is this right? Untick anything that's wrong.
voice.noDose: No dose of {{medicine}} was due today, so it wasn't logged. You can log it from the medicine's page.
